nom: Clinique Moisture Surge Active Glow Serum with Hyaluronic Acid

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin report the serum is surprisingly moisturizing without excess shine, and it can help with winter flakiness while working well under sunscreen.
segments.dry: Dry-skin reviewers, including some with severe or long-standing dryness, report noticeable relief from dryness, smoother texture, and better performance under makeup, especially in cold weather.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers report the serum hydrates well and layers nicely with moisturizer without causing new breakouts.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers largely report good tolerance, hydration, and no burning, though a few note mild redness, stinging, peeling, or that the product is too strong compared to other Clinique items.
segments.mature: Mature-skin reviewers (40s–60s) frequently report a brighter, plumper, more youthful-looking complexion, though one long-time Clinique user found it too strong and irritating for her mature skin.
segments.normal: A reviewer with normal skin found the texture pleasant and moisturizing but did not notice it affecting an existing minor breakout either way.

concerns.aging: Multiple mature reviewers report a brighter, plumper, more youthful appearance and softer skin over weeks of use; one reviewer specifically mentions fine lines appearing less visible.
concerns.dehydration: The large majority of reviewers report meaningful, often fast, relief from dryness and dehydration, including in harsh winter climates; one reviewer felt it gave no extra hydration and would not repurchase.
concerns.redness: One reviewer with existing redness (using Clinique's Redness Solutions line) felt the glow effect was too much and not suited to her skin; another with rosacea reports it gives a flattering glow without issue.
concerns.barrier: Several sensitive or mature reviewers report the serum is gentle and fragrance-free, supporting a compromised barrier, but two reviewers describe stinging, peeling, or skin irritation after use.
concerns.spots: A few reviewers report the serum brightened dark spots, post-acne marks, or hyperpigmentation over time; one reviewer states it did not fade her dark spots much.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers who mention breakouts report none occurred; however, one reviewer noted a few deep chin pimples during the first week and another reviewer's existing minor breakout was unaffected either way.
concerns.oiliness: Oily-skin reviewers report it hydrates without feeling heavy or greasy, and works particularly well layered with sunscreen.

aspects.libelle: Tacky or sticky feel on application
No pilling under makeup or moisturizer

extraits.texte: I used it once earlier this week and the next morning my skin was super stinging. I haven't used it since and my skin is peeling in places. I've been smearing moisture surge all over my face to ease the dryness. While I can see the benefits of it for someone with less mature skin than I, it's like retinol times ten for me.

extraits.titre: Good for my very sensitive skin
extraits.texte: My 56 year old skin is sensitive; no retinoids, retinols, or high percentage vitamin c. They all make me itch, peel and sometimes swell. The lactic acid in this product I can tolerate, and the glycerin is quite nice. It feels a bit tacky until it dries, but I wake up in the morning with smoother, softer skin. I have to take a break every 4th night, and use moisturizer only. It is not fading my dark spots much, but it has helped with smoothing the texture of my skin. Also, as serums go, it is not tremendously overpriced, and I appreciate that. I will repurchase.

This was a small-size tube, part of a Clinique skincare kit. I'm happy to have tried it because it gave my mature dry skin more moisture and a wonderful smooth feel. I didn't find it to be irritating, as I had with another Clinique serum some time ago. In my case though, I think it gave my skin a little too much "glow" as I already have some redness (and use the Redness Solutions line of Clinique products), so it probably isn't the most appropriate for me. Otherwise, I think it is a great addition to the Clinique skincare line.

If you have oily skin that gets flaky in winter or dry this helps alot! And no breakouts. Dont put near your eyes bc it does melt and goes into eyes and really burns. I usually put cheeks below but really hydrates!

extraits.titre: Helps My Other Moisture Surge Products Work Better
extraits.texte: For me, this is a great substitute for Clarifying Lotion, which contain alcohol denat and witch hazel that cause skin irritation. Due to its mild exfoliation, this serum helps my other products absorb into my skin and improves overall moisturization. Hyaluronic acid is a plus. My skin is sensitive and thinning as I age, so I use it only once daily, in the evening. I am cautious about using vitamin C and lactic acid because they can cause stinging and burning, but with once-a-day application followed by moisture surge cream, this hasn't happened. I use sunscreen daily to keep my skin even more protected. I appreciate that Clinique does not use fragrance in their products!
This Vitamin C serum is great for my sensitive and dry skin making it glowy, nourished and healthy. It also brightens dark spots on my face. I have already used the second one.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] I like to examine skincare ingredients before trying a product. The first five ingredients are: water, glycerin, lactic acid, octyldodecyl myristate, and butylene glycol. Overall, these ingredients are quite good, but butylene glycol may not be suitable for those with sensitized skin. Personally, I have sensitive skin, and I found that it handles it well; I experienced a little redness but no burning sensation. Do I feel like I've gained amazing extra hydration? Not really. I probably won't purchase this product again, but it's certainly not the worst I've tried. I do appreciate that it contains lactic acid, which is great for chemical exfoliation. If you're looking for a mild exfoliant with some hydration, I would definitely recommend giving it a try.
